html:
Between 1609 and 1614 King Philip III of Spain expelled the Moriscos, the descendants of Muslims who had been forced to become Christians. About 300,000 people were driven out.

After the conquest of Granada in 1492, Muslims in Castile and then Aragon were made to convert or leave. Many converts kept their language, dress and customs, and some still practised Islam in secret. A revolt in the Alpujarras mountains in 1568 to 1571 was crushed. The church and crown came to see them as a danger, possible allies of the Ottomans and North African corsairs.

The expulsion began in Valencia in 1609, where Moriscos made up about a third of the people, and spread to the rest of Spain. Most went to Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, where they built new communities. It followed the expulsion of the Jews of 1492, and it hurt farming in Valencia and Aragon for decades.
sum: Between 1609 and 1614 King Philip III of Spain expelled the Moriscos, the descendants of Muslims who had been forced to become Christians. About 300,000 people were driven out.
